name: Canopus
description: The brightest and closest yellow supergiant to the Solar System, 95 parsecs away and 73 times the Sun's width.

paper.credit: Domiciano de Souza et al. (2021), A&A 654, A19

radius.source: Domiciano de Souza et al. (2021), A&A 654, A19, Table 3 note and Sect. 5.3: R = 73.2 +/- 3.9 solar radii from the power-law limb-darkened PIONIER diameter 7.184 +/- 0.0017 +/- 0.029 mas and the Hipparcos distance

mass.source: Domiciano de Souza et al. (2021), A&A 654, A19, Table 4: (M/Msun)_Ross = 9.81 +/- 1.83, from the SED fit's log g (1.70 +/- 0.05) and the radius

temperature.source: Domiciano de Souza et al. (2021), A&A 654, A19, Sect. 5.3: Teff 7661 +/- 81 K from the bolometric flux of the SED fit and the PIONIER diameter

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), XHIP, HIP 30438: RV 20.30 +/- 0.50 km/s (quality A)

distance.source: Domiciano de Souza et al. (2021), A&A 654, A19, Sect. 1: d = 94.8 +/- 5.0 pc, the Hipparcos parallax 10.55 +/- 0.56 mas (van Leeuwen 2007) the paper adopts

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

text.card: The brightest and closest yellow supergiant to the Solar System, 73 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: VLTI measured its disc at 7.18 milliarcseconds, which at 95 parsecs is 73.2 solar radii, with 7,661 K at its surface.
